seats.execution: The child finds half of 40 instead of a quarter, splitting it into two equal parts: 40 ÷ 2 = 20. A quarter is one of four equal parts, so 1/4 of 40 is 40 ÷ 4 = 10.
The child works out the dark chocolates correctly, 3/8 of 32 = 12, leaving 20, then takes half of the 20 instead of a quarter: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. A quarter of 20 is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 white chocolates.

Monday uses 3/5 of 40 = 24 litres, leaving 16. On Tuesday the child takes half of the 16 instead of a quarter, 16 ÷ 2 = 8 litres used, and gives the 16 - 8 = 8 left. A quarter of 16 is 4, so 12 litres are left.

The child treats the 140° angle on the line as an angle of the triangle and takes both given angles straight off 180°: 180° - 140° - 30° = 10°. The triangle's own angle there is 180° - 140° = 40°, so the third angle is 180° - 40° - 30° = 110°.

The child treats the 110° angle on the line as an angle of the triangle and takes both given angles straight off 180°: 180° - 110° - 25° = 45°. The triangle's own angle there is 180° - 110° = 70°, so the third angle is 180° - 70° - 25° = 85°.

The child takes the 110° from 180° correctly to get 70°, the triangle's angle next to the line, and gives that as the answer. The question asks for the third angle, so 180° - 70° - 25° = 85° is still to do.
The child counts on from £3.40 to the next pound, £4, a jump of 60p, then on from £4 to £8, a jump of £4, but keeps only the £4 and gives £4.00. The change is both jumps together: 60p + £4 = £4.60.

redrafts.execution: The child turns 1/4 upside down and finds four lots of 40, working out 40 × 4 ÷ 1 = 160. The answer is 40 ÷ 4 × 1 = 10.
The child multiplies 40 by the top number 1 and never divides by the bottom number 4, giving 40 instead of 10. The fraction is treated as the single number 1.
The child takes one quarter of all 32 chocolates, 32 ÷ 4 = 8, instead of a quarter of the 20 left after the dark ones. A quarter of 20 is 5.
The child works out the dark chocolates correctly, 3/8 of 32 = 12, finds the 32 - 12 = 20 left, and gives that. The question asks for the white ones, a quarter of those 20, which is 5.
The child takes Tuesday's quarter of the whole 40 litres, 40 ÷ 4 = 10, instead of a quarter of the 16 litres left after Monday. That gives 16 - 10 = 6 where 16 - 4 is 12.
The child works out Monday correctly, 3/5 of 40 = 24 litres used, and gives the 40 - 24 = 16 litres left. Tuesday is still to do: a quarter of 16 is 4, so 16 - 4 = 12 litres are left.

The child takes the 140° from 180° correctly to get 40°, the triangle's angle next to the line, and gives that as the answer. The question asks for the third angle, so 180° - 40° - 30° = 110° is still to do.

The child finds the triangle's angle on the line correctly, 180° - 140° = 40°, but uses 360° as the total for the triangle: 360° - 40° - 30° = 290°. The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so the third angle is 110°.

The child finds the triangle's angle on the line correctly, 180° - 110° = 70°, but uses 360° as the total for the triangle: 360° - 70° - 25° = 265°. The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so the third angle is 85°.
The child drops the 40p and subtracts whole pounds only: £8 - £3 = £5.00. The book costs £3.40, so the 40p must come off too, leaving £4.60.
The child adds the book's price to the £8 instead of taking it away: £8 + £3.40 = £11.40. Change is what is left, so £8 - £3.40 = £4.60.
